learningObjective: Distinguish weight-only, W8A8, and W4A16 quantization schemes by their memory-traffic and kernel-support profiles.
stem: Consider three inference quantization schemes: (i) weight-only INT4 with FP16 activations (W4A16), (ii) weight-only INT8 with FP16 activations (W8A16), (iii) full W8A8 (weights AND activations INT8). Which statements are TRUE? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: In W4A16, using an INT4 Tensor Core is required for the speedup; without INT4 Tensor Core support, the scheme cannot accelerate anything.
W8A16 is a compute-bound quantization scheme: it uses INT8 Tensor Cores for the matmul and therefore requires an activation calibration pass to determine INT8 activation scales.

W4A16 primarily targets memory-bandwidth-bound decode where the dominant cost is loading weights; the INT4 weights halve HBM traffic vs. INT8, and dequantization to FP16 in-register keeps the compute in FP16 Tensor Cores.
W8A8 targets compute-bound scenarios where an INT8 Tensor Core kernel is available and delivers higher TFLOPS than FP16; activations are quantized dynamically or with a calibrated static scale.

explanation: C: W4A16's design intent is exactly memory-bandwidth-bound decode; INT4 halves weight traffic vs. INT8 while dequant-in-register keeps compute in FP16 Tensor Cores — INT4 Tensor Core hardware is NOT required (contradicting A). D: W8A8 targets compute-bound cases where INT8 Tensor Core throughput dominates and activations can be quantized cheaply. A is false: W4A16 GEMMs typically dequant INT4 to FP16 in registers and use FP16 Tensor Cores. B is false: W8A16 is weight-only quantization; activations stay in FP16, so no activation-calibration step is needed and the matmul uses FP16 Tensor Cores with dequantized weights, not INT8.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: W4A16 does not require INT4 Tensor Cores.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: W8A16 is weight-only — activations stay in FP16, no activation calibration needed, matmul uses FP16 TCs.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: W4A16 memory-bandwidth logic and dequant-in-register.

assumptions: The GPU has FP16 Tensor Core support (Ampere or newer).
The kernel available for W4A16 performs dequant-in-register (typical of Marlin, ExLlama, gptq_gemm).
nonImplications: Does not imply W4A16 beats W8A8 for large-batch prefill (compute-bound); W8A8 can win there.
Does not imply weight-only quantization has zero accuracy cost; it depends on calibration method (RTN, GPTQ, AWQ).

distractorRationales.A: Fabricates a Tensor Core precision requirement.
distractorRationales.B: Confuses weight-only W8A16 with W8A8; the '16' in A16 means FP16 activations.

performanceClaim.scope: Comparative use cases of W4A16 vs W8A8 vs W8A16 on GPU
